title: ML task vocabulary map
description: The search protocol for an ML prior-art survey, built before any searching. It mints the group ids once, records the vocabulary each angle searches on, and gives every registry angle a verdict. It is a PROTOCOL, not a glossary and not a findings document: a claim about what a model or dataset actually does belongs to the search wave, with a source attached.

group_type.description: The AXIS a group sits on. Each angle declares which axes it searches (`applicable_group_types` in the registry), and the coverage grid is keyed on (group x source) — so an axis no angle searches is dead weight, and an angle input no axis covers is an unreachable query. `method` carries architecture and training-approach terms with model SCALE as expansions; vendors are deliberately NOT an axis, because the vendors ARE registry sources and minting a group would put the same names in two places.

sanitization.description: Every source here is a fetched third-party page, and this records that the fetch was treated as DATA. Required on every active source: a posture asserted only in prose is not enforced by anything.

status.description: `clean` nothing was stripped. `modified` something was stripped, and `cause` says what class. `unavailable` the sanitizer could not run — a real state, not a pass. `not-fetched` the posture was established without retrieving a body (from response headers, say), so there was nothing to sanitize.

cause.description: Required for every status but `clean`. What was stripped, or why the sanitizer could not run.

schema_version.description: The version THIS schema validates. A const, not a floor: a minimum would silently judge a v2 artifact against v1 rules, which is the one failure a version field exists to prevent.

retrieved_at.description: When THIS map was built. Distinct from any source's own dates.

revision.description: Monotonic. A protocol is never silently rewritten.

scope_ref.description: The project this survey is FOR, in the words it was handed to you. Every angle verdict is judged against this and `assumptions`; without them a reviewer has nothing to check a verdict against and is pushed toward guessing.

groups.description: The search vocabulary, one entry per (axis, term) the survey will search on. Ids are minted HERE and nowhere else: two angles spelling one group two ways produces two rows for one thing and the dedupe never fires.

id.description: Lowercase kebab-case, unique across the map.

canonical.description: The term this group is FOR, in its most standard form. For an `ml-task` group this is the HuggingFace `pipeline_tag` verbatim.

borrowed_from.description: The vocabulary `canonical` was taken from, when it was taken rather than chosen — `huggingface-pipeline-tag` for an ml-task group. A borrowed name that is not marked as borrowed reads as ours, and then nobody re-checks it when the upstream vocabulary moves.

expansions.description: The other ways this thing is named — vendor synonyms, domain words, and for a `method` group its model-scale variants. Queried alongside the canonical, because a corpus that never uses your word is a corpus you never reach.

expansion_cap.description: The most expansions any one query may carry. Recorded because an unbounded expansion set turns one query into an unreviewable sweep.

negative_terms.description: Terms that make a hit NOT this group — the homonyms. `transformer` reaches electrical engineering; `bert` reaches a muppet.

probe.description: The cheap check that the vocabulary reaches anything at all, before nine angles are dispatched against it. A map whose terms return nothing is a protocol failure, and it is far cheaper to find here.

note.description: What was probed and what came back. A recorded zero here is a finding about the vocabulary, not about the corpus.

excluded.description: Terms and areas considered and deliberately left out, with reasons. Silence and considered exclusion look identical downstream, which is why the record exists.

absent_types.description: Axes this scope genuinely has none of, listed so their emptiness reads as a decision rather than an oversight. A scope with no regulatory exposure has no `harm-category` groups, and saying so is evidence.

angle_applicability.description: One verdict per registry angle, including the ones that do not hold. An angle that never ran and an angle that ran and found nothing are different facts, and only a recorded verdict distinguishes them before the search wave starts.

precondition.description: The angle's trigger, transcribed from the source registry: the same wording and the same set membership, not a paraphrase. Line breaks may fall differently — a folded scalar cannot be re-emitted byte-for-byte and is not expected to be.

holds.description: The precondition evaluated over THE SCOPE — the project this survey is for. Not 'is this angle worth running', and NOT 'does some model in the corpus satisfy it': the corpus is a survey target, the precondition is a statement about the scope. An ALWAYS-ON angle can never be false; it has no precondition to fail.

reason.description: Why `holds` has that value, in terms of the SCOPE. It must name the scope fact and the set. For a disjunctive precondition it must account for the leg that DECIDES the verdict — establishing one leg and reporting the verdict of another is the commonest way a verdict contradicts its own reason. Restating the precondition is not a reason.

sources.description: What this map reached at wave 0. `active` is what the angles may cite; a source that is not active here cannot appear in a coverage cell, which is what makes 'active source' a map STATUS rather than each angle's private opinion.

release.description: The corpus version this source was at. Null when it publishes none — recorded explicitly, because an absent version is a fact about the source.

as_of.description: When the corpus content was true, not when you fetched it. Null when the source states none.

access_status.description: How it answered. `rate-limited` is a normal operating condition for at least one source in this corpus and is never a searched zero.

skipped.description: Registry sources deliberately not reached at wave 0, with the cause. A source that an APPLICABLE angle declares and that appears in neither list is unaccounted for — and an unaccounted source is invisible to the owed set rather than merely absent from it.

assumptions.description: Readings of the SCOPE you had to choose between. Distinct from `notes`, which is about the corpus.

notes.description: Observations about the CORPUS found while building the map — a source URL that moved again, a vocabulary missing a vendor's actual terms. Without this a map-level finding has to be pushed into a search output, which is the wrong document.

lineage.description: Where this map came from, when it was not built from scratch. An amended map that does not say what it amended cannot be diffed against its predecessor.
